newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tells shops to shut early to save power.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tells shops to shut early to save power.

text.p: Bangladesh, facing a severe power shortage, has ordered shops to close by 7 p.m. to reduce outages at homes and factories, energy ministry officials said on Thursday.
They said authorities on Wednesday issued a directive asking shops to close early for the next three months.
Food and medicine shops will, however, be exempted from the restriction.
"This is a temporary measure. We will relax it as soon as the power situation improves," an energy ministry official told Reuters on Thursday.
Bangladesh, facing dwindling gas supplies to power plants, currently produces 1,650 megawatts of electricity. The minimum evening-hour demand is 2,200 megawatts, energy ministry officials said.
They expect gas supplies to be replenished by June.
The energy ministry official said the reduced shopping hours were expected to save between 100 and 150 megawatts.
Existing rules in Bangladesh allow shops to remain open till 8 p.m. but shopkeepers often stay open longer.
